title: Lethal Weapon
build: PAL disk release in a G64 image whose title program is the file LOADER (no file TITLE, which the game-over code asks for); three parts: the title and character select, the game at stage 1A played as Riggs, and the ending

The title program's first instruction, run after the boot file F loads LOADER here. Banks the KERNAL in ($01=$36) and resets the I/O, then loads its files with its own fast loader ($C38A): LOGO at $5800 (the logo's sprites), MUSI at $E000 (the music), which it starts with tune 0, TCHR at $6000, SCN0 at $8000, PORT at $8400, TTHR at $8C00 and TCOL at $A000. Then points the IRQ at $C6E0 for line $30, turns on all eight sprites, picks VIC bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) with the screen at $4000 and characters at $6000, clears both screens and colour RAM, prints the four lines of the title text ($C632) and waits for fire.

Fire was pressed: blanks the screen, sets the IRQ to $C9CE (the music alone) for line $30, takes the sprites away, copies the select screen from $8000 to $4400 and its two character sets from $8400-$93FF to $4800-$57FF, colours each cell from the table at $A007 by its character, sets the four colours from $A003-$A006, and waits.

The character select. Reads both joysticks ($C932) and, until fire is held with left or right, switches the character set by the raster: $D018 = $12 (characters at $4800) above line $10 and below $C0, $14 ($5000) between, so the two portraits use 512 characters.

Fire with a direction: right picks Riggs ($FFF1=1, $FFF2=0), left Murtaugh ($FFF1=0, $FFF2=3). Starts tune 2, loads GAM0 at $03C0 and GAM1 at $E000 over the music, and jumps to $03C0, the game. Nothing in the game reads $FFF2.
The fast loader, the same code as the game's $03C3 at another address: loads the file named at ($BB) (length in $B7) at X/Y, with the KERNAL banked in for the drive commands.
A name starting "$" is not loaded: this JMP goes to the RTS at $C3D7.

238 bytes of 1541 drive code, the same as the game's at $0416, uploaded to the drive's $0600 by $C4C6 and started at $06C7. Its JMPs and JSRs name the drive's own ROM ($F50A, $F8E0 ...) and RAM ($0604, $0680), not the C64's.

The title's copy of the game's $0504: opens the file through the KERNAL to find it, uploads the drive code at $C3D8, then receives the file two bits at a time through $DD00 ($C5xx), storing each byte with every ROM and the I/O banked out.
The drive commands "M-W" and "M-E" with the drive address $06C7.
The file was found: uploads the drive code at $C3D8 in 32-byte M-W blocks to drive $0600-$06FF, starts it with M-E, and receives the file.
Reads the two-byte load address of a block from the drive (the title's copy of the game's $0606).
Receives one byte from the drive, two bits at a time through $DD00 (the title's copy of $0621).
Stores a byte with all ROMs and the I/O banked out (the title's copy of $0665).
The Ocean logo for the title's bottom right corner: 40 character codes, four rows of ten, which $C160 copies to rows 21-24, columns 28-37, of both screens in light blue.
The Ocean logo's second row of characters.
The Ocean logo's third row of characters.
The Ocean logo's fourth row of characters.

The title's four lines, each ending 0, printed by $C915: "LETHAL WEAPON, CHARACTERS, NAMES AND ALL", "   RELATED INDICIA ARE TRADEMARKS OF", "     WARNER BROS., COPYRIGHT 1992." and "PRESS FIRE TO START".
The step in the logo's colour tables, cleared by $C145 and counted up by $C8B0.

Raster interrupt at line $30, the first of the title's chain: flips the shown screen ($D018 bit 4), sets the eight sprite pointers of both screens ($60-$67 and $68-$6F), and places LETHAL's first row at line $48, moving each sprite's x (the words at $C98A, 24 pixels apart) 5 pixels left a frame while the slide lasts; a sprite still beyond the right edge is parked at 0. Sets $C7AC for line $5C.
The operand of the ORA at $C789: written 1 by $C6F7 and shifted left by $C790 for each sprite, the sprite's bit for $D010.
Raster interrupt at line $5C: LETHAL's second row, at line $5D, shown by flipping the screen to the other set of pointers; sets $C7EB for line $72.

Raster interrupt at line $72: flips the screen, sets both screens' pointers to WEAPON's frames ($77 down to $70 and $7F down to $78) and places its first row at line $82, moving each x (the words at $C99A) 4 pixels right a frame while that slide lasts; sets $C8B0 for line $96.
The third row's sprites, one by one: x moved right while the slide lasts, parked at 0 when beyond x 511, line $82.
The operand of this ORA, $00: the bit for the sprite's x high bit, which stays 0 here, so no logo sprite goes past x 255 with its high bit set.
Raster interrupt at line $96: WEAPON's second row at line $97, by flipping the screen, and the next interrupt.
Prints a zero-terminated string from ($2A) to ($28) as screen codes: letters less $40, digits less $30, the rest as 0.
Reads both joystick ports at once into $C96F as the game's $F314 does: up $08, down $04, left $02, right $01, fire $10.
The joysticks as $C932 read them.
The logo's sprite multicolour 0 for each step of its colour sequence ($D025), ending with a negative byte.
The logo's sprite multicolour 1 for each step ($D026).
Eight words: the x of each sprite of the logo's first row, 24 pixels apart, moved by $C6E0.
The high bytes of the first logo row's x words.
The first row's eighth sprite's x, low byte, which $C743 compares with $E0 to end the slide.
Its high byte.
Eight words: the x of each sprite of the logo's third row, 24 pixels apart, moved by $C7AC.
The high bytes of the third logo row's x words.
The third row's eighth sprite's x, low byte, compared with $48 at $C84E to end that slide.
Its high byte, the last of the table.
The names of the files the title loads, four letters each: LOGO, TCHR, SCN0, PORT, TCOL, TTHR, GAM0, GAM1, MUSI.
The select screen's raster interrupt at line $32: plays the music ($E003) and nothing else.
Mark Cooksey's music driver, from the file MUSI. Starts tune A (0, 1 or 2): jumps to $E628.

Plays one frame of music for all three voices, from the title's raster interrupts: counts each voice's note down; at the end of a note reads the next from its stream, a note number (plus the voice's transposition) and a byte giving its length (through $E662) and its instrument; codes from $60 are commands ($E39F), $6B stopping the music. Then works each voice's instrument: pulse-width sweep, vibrato, arpeggio (tables at $E890), waveform changes and the gate, and writes frequency, pulse and control; then sweeps the filter cutoff for the tune ($E8B1-$E8BD).
The low byte of this LDA operand, the arpeggio table address, written by $E239 from $E762.
The high byte of this LDA's operand, the arpeggio table's address, written from $E76D by $E23F (the low byte at $E246 from $E762).
A command in a note stream: $6B stops the music and gates all three voices off; others set a value through a short table and a length.
The low byte of the JMP operand at $E3BA, written by $E3AA from $E552.
The high byte of the JMP at $E3BA's operand, the command routine, written by $E3B0 from $E55D (the low byte by $E3AA from $E552).
Command $60: the next byte is a length code; the next note is tied to this one (not struck again).
Command $61, reached from the table at $E552.
Command $62: sets $E510 from the stream.
Command $63: sets the filter mode bits ($E50F), written to $D418 with the volume.
Command $65: a repeat count for the voice ($E50C), then as command $64.

Command $64: plays a pattern: the next bytes are its number and a transposition; keeps the return place in $E4D3/$E4D6 and its start in $E4DF/$E4E2, and goes to the pattern's address from $F3E5/$F3E8.
Command $66, the end of a pattern: plays it again while the repeat count lasts, otherwise returns to the stream after the call, with the transposition cleared.
Command $67: goes back to the voice's first note ($E4D9/$E4DC), so the tune loops.
Command $68: jumps to the address in the next two bytes.
Command $69: sets the voice's portamento ($E549, $E54C).
Command $6A: picks a filter sweep from the tables at $E8AD-$E8BD.

The work of $E000: takes tune A's three note-stream addresses from $E8C1 and $E8CA (three a tune), gives each voice a first count of 2, silences the SID, sets the volume to 15 and turns the player on ($E4C6).
The operand of this ADC, written by $E628 with the tune number, so X becomes three times the tune: its first voice's place in $E8C1.
The length of a note in frames for each of the 16 length codes in a note's second byte.
